narrative.overview: A worried owner calls from a driveway in daylight, so the site behaves like a neighbour's porch: soft edges, warm linen ground, navy ink spoken calmly, and a single gold hand offered in greeting. Pure white appears only inside cards. Depth comes from diffuse light, never hard offsets. The design's whole job is making the act of handing over the vehicle's details feel safe.
keyCharacteristics: Warm linen ground; white only inside cards
Navy does the talking, gold does the greeting

rules.name: The Porch Light Rule
rules.body: Gold appears once per region: a single action or a small set of icons. It marks the door, so it is never used for two competing actions.

rules.name: The Tinted-Not-Gray Rule
rules.body: Secondary text tints from navy (#55607a) and reads AA on linen. Any flat neutral gray on the warm ground is wrong.

rules.name: The Calm Voice Rule
rules.body: Headlines bind in sentence case with soft tracking. Never condensed capitals or tracked display type.

rules.name: The Soft Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow has a real blur and a small negative spread; a hard offset block or a zero-blur halo never ships here.

dos: Do keep the page ground warm (#fbf7f1); pure white appears only inside cards and panels.
Do place the gold action once per region and give it 50%+ weight in focus.
Do round every corner; the radius ladder is 12/16/20/26/32px and unstated values default upward.
Do set photography with a navy wash strong enough that white type at 4.5:1 minimum is guaranteed where words land.
donts: Don't ship a kicker or eyebrow over any heading; the heading carries its own weight.
Don't use hard offset or stamp shadows, gradient text, glass, or condensed caps — the porch reads calm, not mechanical.
Don't add stat counters, rating badges, or review gadgets; the trust story is the human review, plain words and the phone.
